market.what: PGM (Pt+Pd) content of world oilfield produced water; none is recovered or sold today
market.method: est. ~290 Mbbl/d water (250-328 cited) = 16.8 bn m3/yr x ~1 ng/L PGM (Bakken below detection; reducing brines <0.1 ppb) = ~17 kg/yr x ~$42/g

value.logic: 1 ng/L = $0.04 of PGM per 1,000 m3 water vs ~$1/bbl ($6/m3) handling and >$0.05/m3 sorbent contact cost; even 100x richer water does not pay
value.revenue_logic: no buyer: metal value per m3 below cost of contact; only a niche if a field shows ug/L PGM (none found)
value.margin_logic: moot; would be a specialty grafted resin if any demand appeared

trend.drivers: Permian water 20 Mbbl/d (2024) to 26 Mbbl/d by 2030; disposal limits push reuse and mineral recovery (Li, Br, I), not PGMs

competition.paper_query: platinum group metals oilfield produced water
competition.notes: No one targets PGMs in produced water; brine-mineral startups chase Li/I/Br (Element3 Series A; Altillion $5M seed)

lab.synth: grafted resin: thiol/thiourea ligand on polymer or silica bead, because ng/L capture needs a solid sorbent
lab.test: field assay of real produced water for Pt/Pd first (ICP-MS after preconcentration), then spiked-brine column uptake at 100k+ mg/L TDS; university ICP-MS lab
lab.logic: resin 12 wk + tests 2 wk; resin $25k + ~100 ICP-MS with preconcentration x $80 + water sampling/shipping ~$7k

sale.gates: first prove a field with recoverable PGM (none known); pilot skid on SWD site 1 yr; refiner offtake for loaded resin
